wolfram.note: IsSquareFree itself is correct even for large individual integers (spot-checked up to 9973^2) — hardened it anyway to route plain integers through this package's own factorInteger and decline instead of silently answering False when compute-engine's native factoring gives up (fixed, see backlog.test.ts). But the row's actual failure is in Filter/Range over a large collection: Length(Filter(Range(1,n), IsSquareFree)) is correct up to n=1678 and collapses to a near-empty result exactly at n=1679 (1678 = 2*839, and the correct count at 1678 is exactly 1024 = 2^10 — a suspicious power-of-two buffer/chunk-size limit in the lazy-collection/Filter machinery). That's a collection-iteration bug in the generic evaluation machinery, not in IsSquareFree, and out of scope for this arithmetic-scoped lane; flagging for whoever owns Filter/collection materialization (possibly the same lazy-Range-materialization issue found in the LCM/FoldList rows below).
